key_insight: Se/ZnMgO photodiodes act as self-powered visual synapses whose weight can be potentiated or depressed purely by light wavelength, enabling zero-bias learning and readout.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a low-energy route to neuromorphic vision hardware that integrates sensing, memory, and computation in one flexible optoelectronic device.
method: Built Se/ZnMgO thin-film photodiodes operated at zero bias as artificial synapses
Used wavelength-selective optical pulses and light soaking to map potentiation/depression behavior
Interpreted the mechanism with optical simulations and drift-diffusion modeling of interfacial defect states
evidence_signal: At equal photon flux, 365 nm light increased photocurrent by 38% while 455 nm light decreased it, with up to 19 distinguishable levels per branch and digit-recognition accuracy of 89% ideal / 85% with measured noise.
watch_item: Performance depends on interfacial defect populations and optical conditions, so reproducibility and long-term stability may be sensitive to fabrication variability and device aging.
paper_title: Wavelength-selective bidirectional plasticity in self-powered Se/ZnMgO visual synapses
